;Arts and culture
*[[List of changes made due to the George Floyd protests]]
**[[United States Secretary of Defense]] [[Mark Esper]] issues a new  Department policy that effectively bans the display and depiction of the [[Modern display of the Confederate battle flag#Revival and controversy|Confederate flag]] at any U.S. military installation around the world. "The flags we fly must accord with the military imperatives of good order and discipline, treating all our people with dignity and respect, and rejecting divisive symbols," wrote the Secretary. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-global-race-usa-pentagon/pentagon-issues-de-facto-ban-on-confederate-flag-at-military-bases-idUSKCN24I23K (Reuters)] [https://www.cnn.com/2020/07/17/politics/esper-pentagon-flag-policy/index.html (CNN)]

;Business and economy
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
**[[President of Mexico|President]] [[Andrés Manuel López Obrador]] announces he will donate a quarter of his [[US$]]4,806 monthly salary to help health services fight [[coronavirus disease 2019|the virus]]. He also encouraged other public officials to follow his move. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mexico-politics/mexicos-president-to-donate-part-of-salary-to-coronavirus-effort-idUSKCN24I2H4?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[India]] surpasses one million cases, as the death count reaches 25,000. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-53440913 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Tokyo]] reports a record daily increase in [[COVID-19]] cases, with 293 new cases. [https://www.voanews.com/covid-19-pandemic/tokyo-once-again-sets-daily-record-new-covid-19-cases (Voice of America)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kazakhstan]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Kyrgyzstan]]
****[[Kyrgyzstan]] announces the addition of thousands of cases and hundreds of deaths to its COVID-19 tallies, describing the corresponding [[pneumonia]]-related cases, which had not been confirmed by tests, as most likely linked to the [[SARS-CoV-2]] novel coronavirus. Neighboring [[Kazakhstan]] announces it will do the same starting next month. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-kazakhstan-kyrgyzs/kazakhstan-kyrgyzstan-to-report-some-pneumonia-cases-as-covid-19-idUSKCN24I1DH (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
****[[Manhattan Beach, California|Manhattan Beach]] announces it will fine people who do not wear [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|masks]]. [https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2020-07-17/manhattan-beach-will-fine-those-not-wearing-masks-in-public-the-latest-city-to-do-so?_amp=true (''Los Angeles Times'')]
****[[Governor of California|California Governor]] [[Gavin Newsom]] lays out new rules for schools with high COVID-19 rates to do virtual learning and close campuses until they meet certain health standards. [https://www.politico.com/states/california/story/2020/07/17/newsom-mandates-virtual-instruction-in-most-california-counties-for-now-1301843 (''Politico'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Florida]]
****Officials in [[Miami]] announce that they will impose a [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns#United States|curfew]] at [[South Beach]] as [[Florida]] tops 10,000 cases. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/florida-county-imposes-curfew-as-coronavirus-cases-spike-2020-07-17/ (CBS News)]
***Military medics are deployed to hospitals in [[Texas]] and [[California]] as cases surge. [https://www.chicagotribune.com/coronavirus/ct-nw-coronavirus-updates-20200717-5aqubheiezgjnmshtj2rxz36oq-story.html?outputType=amp (''The Chicago Tribune'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] state reports a record daily increase in COVID-19 cases, with 428 new cases and three new deaths. Australia in overall records 438 new cases, highest since mid-March. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-australia/in-the-fight-of-our-lives-australia-posts-surge-in-new-covid-19-cases-idUSKCN24I08U (Reuters)] [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2020-07-17/victoria-coronavirus-cases-update-record-covid19-daily-increase/12465632 (ABC News (Australia))]

;International relations
*[[Egypt–Turkey relations]], [[Turkey–United Arab Emirates relations]], [[Second Libyan Civil War]]
**[[Turkish President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] denounces [[Egypt]] and the [[United Arab Emirates]] for supporting the eastern-based [[Libya]]n forces of [[Khalifa Haftar]]. [[Turkey]] says it will maintain its support for the [[Government of National Accord]] (GNA) and calls the UAE's actions "piratical". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-libya-security-turkey-egypt/turkeys-erdogan-says-egypts-actions-in-libya-are-illegal-idUSKCN24I1MN (Reuters)]
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
**South Korea revokes licenses to anti-Pyongyang groups which often send leaflets to the border with political messages. The South Korean government says these groups are "seriously hindering the unification policy of the government". The groups accuse the government of censorship. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/south-korea-revokes-licences-propaganda-balloon-groups-200717151057753.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Law and crime
*[[United States racial unrest (2020–2023)|United States racial unrest]]
**[[George Floyd protests]]
***[[List of George Floyd protests in the United States|George Floyd protests in the United States]]
****[[George Floyd protests in Illinois]]
*****[[George Floyd protests in Chicago]]
******Protesters attempt to remove a [[Statue of Christopher Columbus (Chicago)|statue]] of [[Christopher Columbus]] at [[Grant Park (Chicago)|Grant Park]], prompting a standoff with police. [https://www.newsweek.com/chicago-christopher-columbus-statue-center-protest-police-clash-1518807 (''Newsweek'')]
**[[Breonna Taylor protests]]
***Prosecutors drop felony charges against 87 people who protested the [[Breonna Taylor]] [[Shooting of Breonna Taylor|police killing]] outside of [[Attorney General of Kentucky|Kentucky Attorney General]] [[Daniel Cameron (Kentucky politician)|Daniel Cameron]]’s home. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/07/17/us/breonna-taylor-louisville-protests.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Iran]]ian [[Law Enforcement Force (Iran)|police]] disperse [[2019–2020 Iranian protests |protesters]], who this week marched against the [[capital punishment in Iran|death sentence]] upon three political activists, and vow to "decisively" deal with further protests. The protesters march under the slogan "[[StopExecutionsinIran|#StopExecutionsinIran]]". [https://www.dw.com/en/iran-death-penalty-masih-alinejad/a-54222035 (DW)]
*[[Law enforcement in Germany|Police]] in [[Germany]] arrest a gunman, nicknamed Rambo due to his acts, who disarmed four policemen and escaped in the [[Black Forest]] five days before. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53451478 (BBC News)]
